"""PLANTED NEGATIVE CONTROL -- the shell half, done correctly.

Same rung, same interpreter fallback, one difference: a `_native` header
probe runs first and execs the image directly when the bytes say it is one.
That is the shell spelling of the magic-byte refusal, and it is what the
live generated hook carries today. Flagging this file would RED already-fixed
code. `.py.txt` so nothing else reads it.
"""


def hook_body(script_name):
    settings_home_script = (
        '${COORDINATOR_SETTINGS_HOME:-$HOME/.coordinator-claude-settings}/bin/'
        f'{script_name}'
    )
    return (
        "#!/bin/sh\n"
        '_native() { head -c 4 "$1" 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C grep -q "[^[:print:][:space:]]"; }\n'
        '_PY=python3\n'
        f'_T="{settings_home_script}"\n'
        'if _native "$_T"; then exec "$_T" "$@"; fi\n'
        'exec "$_PY" "$_T" "$@"\n'
    )
